correctness.rationale: After translating a root query to zero, its positive centers are edges. Within that fiber only queries of weights 0, 2 and 4 can be positive. A weight-four positive fiber has at most six edges; a weight-two positive fiber is a two-star. In a two-star, a weight-four or disjoint weight-two query has at most four positives; a pair containing exactly one hub splits it into two near-stars. A near-star query always has one branch of size at most three, which excludes depth three. Thus the edge class has rank at most four and the whole class at most five, also for small dimensions and duplicate concepts. All 32 supplied seven-bit witnesses and, separately, all possible masks over the 128 seven-bit centers were checked by independent code without executing the shipped verifier. Zero padding preserves the lower bound. The finite calculation proves the stated witness only; the edge-fiber argument gives the universal upper bound.
